entries.set_purpose: One unloaded reach/return cycle rehearses the stable trunk and comfortable arm path used in the upcoming chest release. It introduces vocabulary for upper-body setup; it does not assess pressing strength or rowing skill.
entries.prior_current_next: Actual OR-01/04 or direct equivalent trunk/conduct record → one specific unloaded chest-start rehearsal → P2 handling and E1 first release only when their separate readiness is present.
entries.advance_hold_regress: Hold the comfortable range and easy effort. Stop/reduce the affected action for pain, loss of control or inability to follow the cue; age and date do not authorize a harder variant.

standard_D.variant: Unloaded Chest-Start Reach and Return — stationary bilateral teaching task
standard_D.effort_load: Unloaded, easy 1–2/10; one comfortable bilateral forward reach and return. Both feet stay planted, no dip, arch, step, jump or forced end range.
standard_D.notes: One whole counted action per set. Phase times are coaching envelopes, not a demand to rush. P2 never releases a ball; E1 attempts, including faults, use their listed opportunity. No bonus trials.

entries.set_purpose: One counted no-release handling set adds the actual implement and known instruction to a stable position. It teaches grip, waiting, comfortable floor pickup/set-down and a short controlled carry without hiding an extra throw or separate assessment inside preparation.
entries.prior_current_next: Actual OR-01/04 equipment and upper-body setup evidence → one counted ball-start hold with no release → E1 teaches the known release/retrieval; OR-09 later keeps the actual mastered implement and changes cue interpretation only.
entries.advance_hold_regress: A comfortable controlled floor pickup, hold, short carry and set-down plus an eligible unloaded projection and understood conduct permits instruction of the first counted E1 release and its longer retrieval route. It does not establish repeatable throwing, retrieval, reaction or main-entry competence. Keep the actual ball and position; do not increase mass within the visit.

standard_D.notes: One whole counted action per set. Phase times are coaching envelopes, not a demand to rush. P2 never releases a ball; E1 attempts, including faults, use their listed opportunity. No bonus trials.

entries.set_purpose: Each listed single-throw set has the same purpose: connect a controlled bilateral chest release to one clear early permission cue and then practice the shared retrieval rule. D uses 3 standard / 2 compressed opportunities; L uses 2 / 1, for all ages. This is a low-dose participation lesson in the Explosiveness window, not a maximal power assessment. The first attempt is the counted instructional observation.
entries.prior_current_next: Actual OR-01/04 conduct and upper-body readiness, plus separately established throwing history when available → first or retained stable single release/retrieval under one known early cue → OR-09 may add go/no-go only to the actual repeatable movement at retained ball/stance/direction/intent; OR-13 retains the passed throw/cue route if travel/redirect is unavailable. No jumping, braking, go/no-go or cutting credit follows from this lesson.
entries.advance_hold_regress: Advance toward a repeatable recorded stable-throw and early-release result only when actual attempts show controlled direction, unchanged stance, waiting and retrieval without extra physical prompting, with comfortable response. A few planned attempts are not an automatic pass: retain emerging/unobserved status when evidence is insufficient. Hold the variation and output. Stop all lanes for an unsafe release, moving ball, intrusion or lost cue control; never add a make-up attempt. Pain ends the affected physical task and informs the appropriate professional/coach decision.

entries.set_purpose: A single supported pressing set makes hand placement, body line, comfortable range and controlled finish visible after the throw lesson. The first listed repetition is the counted observation; this is upper-body instruction, not additional throw output.
entries.prior_current_next: Actual OR-01/02/03/04 or direct equivalent push dose, setup and response → one explicit compatible set today (retain one or deliberately reduce two) → OR-09/13 retain actual stable strength while their named cue variable changes; OR-06 retains or changes its own landing/hip anchor independently. Unknown or omitted history is not replaced by the planned D dose.
entries.advance_hold_regress: Retain the actual compatible setup, load, range and listed tempo. Teach an unknown setup within its block and count the first repetition. Reduce to the listed L dose or an independently eligible replacement when current response warrants it; stop an unsuitable action. Throwing success never authorizes heavier pressing/pulling, and shoulder response may require deferral of either role. No missed work is owed.
